identity.name: Ledgerly
identity.description: A bookkeeping assistant for independent creative studios that matches bank-feed transactions to receipts and prepares a month-end close checklist.

capabilities: Suggests matches between imported bank-feed transactions and uploaded receipts
Builds a month-end close checklist from unmatched items
Exports a reconciliation summary for the studio's accountant
limitations: Does not file taxes or replace an accountant
Bank feeds are imported from CSV files; there is no live bank connection
Receipt matching still needs human confirmation
product.positioning: Ledgerly helps small creative studios close their books each month without a dedicated bookkeeper.
differentiation: Close checklist instead of a full ledger
pricing: Private beta: free for invited studios
offers: Guided first month-end close with a Ledgerly specialist

terminology.close: The month-end reconciliation of transactions and receipts

accessibilityConstraints: No information conveyed by colour alone

history.rationale: First complete product truth after the private beta kickoff.

claims.statement: Ledgerly suggests receipt matches for most imported bank-feed transactions; a person confirms each match.
claims.rationale: Private beta usage shows most transactions receive a confirmed suggested match.

claims.statement: Studios finish their month-end close in a single afternoon with Ledgerly.
claims.rationale: Interviews describe the current pain, not the post-Ledgerly duration; needs outcome evidence before approval.

evidence.title: Five studio-owner interviews on month-end close
evidence.summary: Five owners of 3-12 person design studios described spending most of a working day each month matching card transactions to receipts.

evidence.title: Private beta receipt-matching usage
evidence.summary: Across 14 private beta studios, 71% of imported transactions had a suggested receipt match confirmed by a person within the same week.

evidence.title: Freelancer forum thread about invoice chasing
evidence.summary: A public thread where solo freelancers say chasing unpaid invoices hurts more than reconciliation. Not yet checked for representativeness.

evidence.title: Agency pricing objection notes
evidence.summary: Sales notes from three agency calls: owners would pay for the close checklist but objected to per-seat pricing.

icpHypotheses.name: Independent design studios (3-15 people)
icpHypotheses.summary: Owner-led design studios that pay for projects on shared cards and close their books monthly without a bookkeeper.

problemIntensity.rationale: Interviewed owners lose most of a working day each month to reconciliation.

urgency.rationale: Pain peaks at month end and before quarterly tax estimates.

productFit.rationale: Beta usage shows most transactions receive a confirmed suggested match.

timeToValue.rationale: Value appears in the first close after importing one month of CSV data.

access.rationale: Reachable through design community newsletters and LinkedIn.

proof.rationale: One reviewed usage metric; no published case study yet.

adoptionFriction.rationale: Needs a monthly CSV export from the bank.

commercialViability.rationale: Owners would pay for the checklist but object to per-seat pricing.

retentionPotential.rationale: Monthly close is a recurring job.

strategicFit.rationale: Matches the project-based spending model Ledgerly is built around.

evidenceQuality.rationale: Small interview sample plus beta analytics.

disqualifiers: Studios with an in-house finance team
Studios that do not reconcile monthly
antiIcpConditions: Needs payroll or tax filing inside the product
assumptions: Owners will export a bank CSV each month
contradictions: Two interviewed studios already pay an outside bookkeeper and saw less value
icpHypotheses.nextValidationAction: Interview three more studios that do not use an outside bookkeeper
changeConditions: Fewer than half of new interviewees report monthly reconciliation pain

experiments.hypothesis: Studios without an outside bookkeeper report monthly reconciliation pain
experiments.method: Three 30-minute interviews using the existing interview guide
successCriteria: At least two of three describe monthly reconciliation as a top-three admin pain
failureCriteria: Fewer than two of three describe monthly reconciliation pain
decisionCriteria: Keep or narrow the studio ICP based on the result

history.rationale: Strongest reviewed evidence and the clearest product fit for the beta.

icpHypotheses.name: Solo freelance creatives
icpHypotheses.summary: Individual illustrators and photographers who track income and expenses alone.

problemIntensity.rationale: Forum thread suggests invoicing pain outweighs reconciliation pain.

urgency.rationale: Urgency is seasonal around tax deadlines.

timeToValue.rationale: Small transaction volume means a quick first close.

proof.rationale: Only unreviewed public-source evidence so far.

adoptionFriction.rationale: Many use personal accounts mixed with business spending.

commercialViability.rationale: Low willingness to pay suggested by the thread.

retentionPotential.rationale: Recurring need, but may churn after tax season.

antiIcpConditions: Mixes personal and business spending in one account
icpHypotheses.nextValidationAction: Review the forum evidence, then decide whether to compare this audience with the studio ICP
changeConditions: Reviewed evidence shows reconciliation pain comparable to studios
